summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR 199 million (2.31% margin) on a 3% revenue rise, with Roha plant start-up costs and West Asia disruption driving the squeeze.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 operating income was INR 8,633 million (up about 3% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 199 million at a 2.31% margin and net profit of INR 243 million. For FY26, operating income rose about 7% to INR 29,148 million while EBITDA fell 29% to INR 2,102 million (7.21% margin) and PAT was INR 1,432 million (4.91%). Management attributed the weakness to West Asia crisis disruptions (about Rs 60 crore of deferred GCC engineering exports), input cost inflation (styrene, oleum), Roha plant depreciation and interest, and slow government fund flow on the UP Jal Jeevan project. Management declined to give FY27 sales, margin, or gross debt guidance until the second half of the year.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 5,539 million, flat YoY, with segment EBIT of INR 215 million. Margin fell on about Rs 60 crore of deferred GCC export shipments, a higher mix of domestic shipments, and legacy UP Jal Jeevan project drag; order intake was reported about 40% above last full year.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 2,297 million (up about 3% YoY), EBIT INR 334 million. Management attributed about three-quarters of the segment margin decline (about 4 points on a full-year basis, to ~3% segment EBIT margin) to Roha costs, and the rest to input costs and deferred resin revenue from logistics disruption; Dammam (Saudi Arabia) plant has begun commercial production.

segments.name: Consumer Products
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,047 million (up 34% YoY) with loss narrowed to INR 46 million from INR 52 million; management targets at least breakeven to low single-digit profit.

segments.name: International / Group
segments.commentary: 20-year DBOOT contract from Petroleum Development Oman (OMR 73.46 million) is progressing on schedule via 51%-owned JV, with capex of about USD 40 million over two years. New Malawi water package worth USD 18.1 million awarded via a project JV.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 sales, margin, capex or gross debt guidance given; management plans to guide in the second half of FY27, citing West Asia uncertainty.
Directionally, FY27 sales and margins are expected to improve over the next few months; part of lost Q4 chemicals revenue expected to be recovered in FY27.
Roha plant: management said it remains on track for 25% capacity utilisation in the first full year and expects to meet that in FY27; PBT break-even at Roha targeted but not assured.
Legacy engineering project to be closed within FY27 per management; UP Jal Jeevan project will take at least the next financial year to complete.
FY27 maintenance and routine capex about Rs 30-40 crore; gross debt about Rs 384 crore; no major expansion capex currently envisaged.
Consumer Products: growth to continue at a slightly lower rate; aim to reach at least breakeven or low single-digit profit.
capex_capacity: Roha resin plant (42,600 cubic metre capacity) fully commissioned; all manufacturing lines commissioned in Q4 and major capitalisation in March 2026; backward integration still underway.
Roha WQA (Water Quality Association, US) certification received after the quarter, opening US drinking-water export channels.
Dammam, Saudi Arabia plant started commercial production for Middle East market.
IOCL Panipat Refinery raw water treatment plant commissioned; Sri Lanka project closure expected by end of Q2 FY27.
Oman PDO project capex about USD 40 million over next two years, funded by debt and equity (equity from internal accruals).
demand_pricing: Engineering order inflows grew QoQ and YoY, mainly medium-sized opportunities; order intake reportedly about 40% above last full financial year.
Chemicals turnover hit in March 2026 by West Asia logistics disruption; price increases initiated to pass on higher raw material costs (styrene, oleum).
Roha customers: mix of existing and new customers, OEMs and end-users; products require trials and certifications after full commissioning, so there is a qualification lead time.
Membranes: global membrane market growing 10%-plus CAGR; MANN+HUMMEL tie-up brings PVDF flat-sheet ultrafiltration and MBR technology; competitors named include DuPont, Toray, Veolia, Hydronautics.
Jal Jeevan (UP) fund flows improved after the Union Budget reaffirmed the scheme for four years, but execution pace remains slow with about 30% of scope pending.

qa_highlights.question: Is Roha on track for 25%-30% utilisation and customer acquisition progress; can PBT break-even come this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it remains on track for 25% utilisation in the first full year and should meet it this FY, though styrene and oleum costs are headwinds. Break-even is being pursued but timing depends on the West Asia situation.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the chemicals margin decline is due to Roha versus Middle East logistics and input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Three-quarters of the segment margin decline is from Roha; one-quarter from West Asia, input costs and deferred resin revenue. Roha's impact was just under 7% for Q4 and about 3% segment EBIT margin for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much engineering revenue was affected by the Middle East crisis and legacy projects?
qa_highlights.answer: The West Asia impact on engineering was Rs 60 crore; legacy and UP project effects are said to follow the same ratio as the last few quarters. Management said it would not give a finer split.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex, gross debt and sales/margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No sales or margin guidance until H2 FY27. Maintenance capex Rs 30-40 crore and gross debt about Rs 384 crore; no major capex currently planned without expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the jump in Q4 other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly FOREX gains on exports plus claims on an EPC contract; management did not quantify the split.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Oman project excluded from reported order book?
qa_highlights.answer: The disclosed order inflow and backlog cover only the standalone entity, excluding subsidiary and associate orders.

risks_watch: West Asia crisis: logistics and shipping disruption and raw material costs (styrene, oleum) may persist into Q1 FY27; the company will share more by end of Q1.
Roha profitability: depreciation and interest from the new plant are weighing on chemicals EBIT; utilisation ramp depends on lengthy customer qualifications.
Jal Jeevan (UP) receivables and execution pace depend on government fund flows; about 30% of scope remains.
Engineering margin pressure from the legacy project spilling into FY27 and deferred GCC shipments.
Oman PDO capex (about USD 40 million) and its debt funding could raise group leverage; gross debt is about Rs 384 crore currently.
Q4 other income boosted by FOREX gains and EPC claims, which may not recur.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, membranes and Roha, but cautious and often deferential on near-term numbers: management declined to quantify Q4 chemicals revenue loss, FY27 guidance, and the Jal Jeevan timeline, citing West Asia uncertainty.

We remain in line with those expectations.
We will be in a position to provide more clarity in the second half of the year.
The long-term story remains as bright as it was, and I do not think that is something which we are worried about.
